pa_g_autumn_arch_sector.blurb: Autumn Arch Sector is one of the sport-climbing walls at Safe Harbor South, in Conestoga Township a short drive southwest of Lancaster. It sits between the Super Slab and Train in Vain sectors and holds 20 routes, nearly all of them bolted, with a pair of trad lines. The lines here are among the tallest and steepest at the crag, and the sector is known for its steadier mid-grade pitches around 5.10 plus a handful of 5.11 and 5.12 tests and one 5.13. Easier options exist too, starting near 5.7. Expect a high-profile, busy wall rather than a quiet corner.
pa_g_autumn_arch_sector.parking_note: Leave the car near the railroad tunnel on Green Hill Road, using the pull-offs on either side, then walk up to the old rail bed where the sectors are strung out.

qc_le_gros_bras.blurb: Le Gros Bras is a big cliff in the Charlevoix region, inside Grands-Jardins National Park near the Lac des Cygnes mountain. It is mostly a traditional-climbing venue: 28 of its 29 listed lines are trad, plus a single boulder problem. Many are multi-pitch, running from three up to eight pitches, with a lot of moderate climbing around 5.7 to 5.10 and a few much harder lines at 5.12 and a hard V5 problem. It works as an alpine-style training ground in summer, and in winter a few mixed lines can be climbed when ice does not form. Wet, dirty rock and loose sections are possible, so it suits experienced leaders.

qc_c_h_lios.blurb: Hélios is the third wall along the path at the Chez Roger cliff, in the Lanaudière region of Quebec near Saint-Alphonse-Rodriguez. It carries 29 routes, split fairly evenly between sport and trad, so bring a rack for some of them. The grade spread leans hard: a couple of very easy lines, then mostly 5.10 through 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. This is a place for strong climbers who want steep faces, crimps and the occasional crack, rather than a beginner crag. A helmet is wise on a cliff of this size.

qc_2_left_wall.blurb: Left Wall is the first cliff you meet when walking trail C at La Bleue, near Val-David in the Laurentides. It has a zig-zag shape and 28 routes, almost all of them traditional, with two sport lines. Beginners have a few options (starting around 5.5 and 5.7), while the core of the wall is 5.10 to 5.12, and there are several hard lines up to 5.13. La Bleue as a whole is mostly single-pitch cragging, and tree cover offers some shade in summer.

qc_8_std_wall.blurb: STD Wall is the steepest section of the Mont Rigaud cliff, west of Montreal, on pink granite. Its 27 routes are mostly sport (20), with a few trad lines and three top-rope problems. A pair of very easy climbs and a short run of 5.9 and below are outnumbered by the hard stuff: most routes fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a single 5.13. Ledges break up the face, and an easier top-rope corner called Bonnie's Wall sits off to the right for warming up or taking newcomers. Expect steep, powerful climbing on a wall of modest height.

qc_f_prom_th_e.blurb: Prométhée is the sixth wall along the path at the Chez Roger cliff, in Quebec's Lanaudière region. It is a sport-focused wall: 24 of the 27 routes are bolted, with three trad lines. Every route sits at 5.10 or harder, most of them 5.11 and 5.12, with one 5.13, so it is a good fit for climbers who have already settled into the lower double digits. The walk from the car is under fifteen minutes. Chez Roger as a whole offers steep faces, crimps and overhanging arêtes, and a helmet and stick clip are worth carrying.
